hints: Focus on the overall shape of melting point across a Period 3 sequence, from a Group 1 metal up to the giant covalent peak then a sharp fall.
Notice the very highest peak must be silicon with giant covalent bonding, so count backwards three places to find magnesium, then one more back to sodium.
Check the two points to the left of your sodium candidate, they should be low with the second one even lower, just like a halogen followed by a noble gas.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Period 3 melting point pattern**

Think of the eight elements $\text{Na}$ to $\text{Ar}$ in order. Melting point rises from $\text{Na}$ to $\text{Si}$, then falls sharply.

$$\text{Na (low) < Mg < Al < Si (peak, very high) >> P, S, Cl, Ar (all low)}$$

**Match the peak in the diagram**

The diagram shows a very high peak at the 6th dot. That shape screams giant covalent $\text{Si}$. So the 6th dot is silicon.

This is the anchor for the whole sequence.

**Count back to find sodium**

If dot 6 is $\text{Si}$ (atomic number 14), then count back: dot 5 is $\text{Al}$ (13), dot 4 is $\text{Mg}$ (12), dot 3 is $\text{Na}$ (11).

Dot 3 is labelled C, so C could be sodium.

**Check the left-hand side makes sense**

If C is $\text{Na}$ (11), then B is $\text{Ne}$ (10) and A is $\text{F}$ (9). Both have very low melting points with simple van der Waals forces, and noble gas $\text{Ne}$ is even lower than $\text{F}_2$.

That matches A slightly higher than B, then a rise to C. Everything fits.

options.A: A cannot be sodium because it is the first of the eight dots and is followed by an even lower point B. Sodium is followed by higher melting points (Mg, Al, Si). A fits fluorine, $\text{F}_2$, with low van der Waals forces, just above neon.
options.B: B cannot be sodium because it is the lowest point in the left pair. This is characteristic of a noble gas with very weak instantaneous dipole forces. B fits neon, $\text{Ne}$, which has a lower melting point than both fluorine and sodium.
options.C: C is correct because it sits two places before the Mg-Al plateau and three places before the Si peak. This gives the sequence C = Na, D = Mg, next = Al, next = Si (peak), then a sharp fall to P and S. The rise from B (Ne) to C (Na, metallic bonding) also fits perfectly.
options.D: D cannot be sodium because it is already high up on the rising slope and levels off to the next point. This plateau is Mg to Al, both with stronger metallic bonding than Na. D fits magnesium, not sodium.
